name: Silkworm
label: Touch and Go
lede: Three friends from Missoula and a drummer from Seattle made records for twenty years that critics loved and crowds mostly missed. A driver at a Skokie red light ended it in 2005.

eras.title: Ein Heit in Missoula
eras.text: Silkworm started with teenagers in Missoula, Montana, a long way from any music industry. Before the name came Ein Heit and a couple of self-dubbed cassettes.

years.h: Tim Midyett, Andy Cohen and Joel RL Phelps start playing as Ein Heit
years.p: In Missoula, Montana, the three future Silkworm songwriters make up part of Ein Heit from mid-1985 until June 1987.

years.h: Silkworm starts without one of its three
years.p: Andy Cohen and Joel Phelps get the band going in Missoula in November 1987. Tim Midyett, away at college, joins in June 1988.

years.h: A cassette called Advantage
years.p: Silkworm self-release the demo tape in 1988 and Girl Harbrr in 1989, then move the band to Seattle.

eras.title: Seattle, where nobody came
eras.text: They moved to Seattle just as the rest of the world was about to look there, and still couldn't fill a room. What they got instead was a drummer, Michael Dahlquist, and a producer from their own high school.

years.src: Silkworm.net: Tim's History of Silkworm · Wikipedia: Michael Dahlquist
years.h: Silkworm trade their drum machine for Michael Dahlquist
years.p: Tim Midyett on why Silkworm kept booking Seattle shows after arriving at the start of 1990. Michael Dahlquist, who grew up in nearby Bothell, joins on drums.
years.xp:
Dahlquist met the band in January 1990, when they were looking for a drummer to replace the drum machine, according to Wikipedia.

Midyett's history of the band says he is still amazed by "the endless number of sparsely attended shows" they played in their first four years. They did better in Chicago, New York and San Francisco than at home.

yt: Live at the Middle East Cafe, Cambridge, Oct 28, 1992
years.h: L'ajre comes out on a label called Temporary Freedom
years.p: The debut album follows a run of 7-inch singles that began in 1991.

years.src: Wikipedia · Silkworm.net: Tim's History of Silkworm
years.h: A call to Northwestern's radio station reveals another Hellgate High grad
years.p: While Silkworm are on WNUR, [[Steve Albini|a4d486bd-6020-4a36-9c7d-bf5ce174bcd1]] phones in and they learn he went to Hellgate High School in Missoula too. He produces In the West for C/Z Records, the start of a long partnership.
years.xp: Midyett's history says In the West changed their luck: after it came out it "became easier for us to book shows at good local clubs, and we could attract crowds."

years.big: "I just really didn't want to have to make any choices."
years.src: Vice · Silkworm.net: Tim's History of Silkworm
years.h: Joel RL Phelps quits just before Libertine
years.p: Phelps left in 1994, citing his health and the strain of touring. Tim Midyett wrote that the band found it easy to carry on as a trio.
years.xp:
Phelps told Vice in 2014 that he knew he was struggling with drinking at the time and didn't want to deal with it. "I was drinking all day long, morning noon and night," he said.

He got sober and now volunteers in Vancouver helping people recover from addiction. He is back in Silkworm for the reunion shows.

years.h: Libertine is out, and Phelps is already gone
years.p: Released on El Recordo, it's the last album with Joel Phelps. Comedy Minus One reissued it in May 2014 as a 2×12-inch with bonus tracks.

eras.title: A trio on Matador
eras.text: Down to three, Silkworm signed to Matador and got onto real tours. Steve Albini kept recording them, in Seattle and at his own house.

years.src: Silkworm.net: Tim's History of Silkworm · Wikipedia
years.h: Firewater puts a three-piece Silkworm on tour with Pavement
years.p: The first album as a trio comes out on Matador in spring 1996, and the band tours with [[Pavement|36bfa85f-737b-41db-a8fc-b8825850ffc3]] and [[Guided by Voices|6c85f4c3-026c-4c16-9a7c-f546f42ed0fb]]. Comedy Minus One announced an expanded 2xLP reissue for December 4, 2026.
years.xp: Midyett's history says Firewater sold better than what came before and got them onto tours with bigger bands. After 1994, touring took up several months of every year.

years.h: Albini records Developer in a Seattle studio and in his own house
years.p: Steve Albini cuts Silkworm's Developer at Robert Lang Studios in Seattle and at his home.
years.xp: Midyett has described the songs as "weird, bendy, lugubrious, hyper," with basslines that are "2/3rds passing tones." Paul Tremblay, writing about the album, called it "a film noir album."

eras.title: Touch and Go lifers
eras.text: From 1998 Silkworm made four albums for Touch and Go: praised, steady, never a hit. Matt Kadane of Bedhead played keyboards on the later ones.

years.h: Blueblood moves Silkworm to Touch and Go
years.p: It's the band's first album for Touch and Go. The same year, Matador rounds up the early singles as Even a Blind Chicken Finds a Kernel of Corn Now and Then: 1990–1994.

years.h: The Crust Brothers put Stephen Malkmus in a covers band
years.p: Michael Dahlquist and Silkworm play covers with [[Stephen Malkmus|eaefd603-84c1-4db4-a72b-0cb718a0cc07]] as The Crust Brothers. The live album Marquee Mark comes out in 1998.

years.h: Two years on, Lifestyle
years.p: The second of the band's four albums for Touch and Go, out in 2000 between Blueblood and Italian Platinum.

years.h: Bedhead's Matt Kadane adds keyboards to Italian Platinum
years.p: [[Matt Kadane|7449c305-8a29-46e1-8934-ced2f4f7e6ef]] of Bedhead joins Silkworm in the studio. The You Are Dignified EP follows on 12XU in 2003.

years.h: It'll Be Cool ends the Touch and Go run
years.p: It's the last Silkworm album with Michael Dahlquist on drums, and the band's last for Touch and Go.

eras.title: A red light on Dempster Street
eras.text: A driver trying to kill herself ran a red light and hit the car carrying Michael Dahlquist and two other Chicago musicians. Silkworm ended there, and the court case ran three more years.

years.src: Wikipedia: Jeanette Sliwinski · Wikipedia: Michael Dahlquist
years.h: A Mustang runs a red light on Dempster Street and kills Michael Dahlquist
years.p: In Skokie, Illinois, Jeanette Sliwinski drives at high speed into the car carrying Silkworm drummer Dahlquist, 39, and musicians Douglas Meis and John Glick. All three die.
years.xp:
According to Wikipedia, Sliwinski had argued with her mother and was trying to kill herself; she had been hospitalized for psychiatric care two weeks earlier. Both cars flipped, and Meis died ten minutes after reaching the hospital.

She was arrested in her hospital room the next day and charged with three counts of first-degree murder and two of aggravated battery. Meis played in the Dials and EXO, Glick in the Returnables.

years.h: Bottomless Pit grows out of what's left of Silkworm
years.p: 12XU releases the Chokes! EP as a Silkworm record. Tim Midyett and Andy Cohen carry on as [[Bottomless Pit|b427ea89-6351-4e61-8f76-74d7b7ecf295]], which runs until an indefinite hiatus in 2014.

years.h: Jeanette Sliwinski is convicted of reckless homicide, not murder
years.p: She had pleaded not guilty by reason of insanity and is acquitted of first-degree murder in the Skokie crash. The sentence is eight years.
years.xp: Her trial began October 15, 2007. She was eligible for parole after 19 months and was paroled October 2, 2008, having served about three years, with her sentence reduced by Illinois law, time served, good behavior and counseling credits.

eras.title: Couldn't you wait?
eras.text: A documentary made the case for Silkworm to people who'd missed them. Then Steve Albini's death brought three of them back on stage, with Joel Phelps singing for the first time since 1994.

yt: Trailer for Couldn't You Wait? The Story of Silkworm
years.h: Jeff Tweedy, Steve Albini and Stephen Malkmus talk Silkworm on film
years.p: Couldn't You Wait? The Story of Silkworm, a documentary on the band, premieres in February 2013.

years.h: Steve Albini dies of a heart attack at 61
years.p: He had recorded Silkworm from In the West on and gone to their Missoula high school. He died at his Chicago home.

years.h: Joel Phelps sings with Silkworm for the first time since 1994
years.p: Silkworm play a tribute concert for Steve Albini. Jeff Panall of [[Songs: Ohia|1305bd7e-27ef-4236-ae87-0a7d435234ca]] and Mint Mile takes Michael Dahlquist's place on drums.

years.src: Comedy Minus One: Developer reissue · Pitchfork: Silkworm to reunite for 2025 shows
years.h: Developer gets a second life as a 1,000-copy 2xLP
years.p: Comedy Minus One's expanded reissue adds a Bob Dylan cover with Stephen Malkmus of Pavement. Pitchfork reports Silkworm will reunite for more shows in 2025.
years.xp: The reissue came out February 21, 2025, on 150-gram vinyl, with six bonus tracks added to the original 1997 album: five Japan-exclusive songs that had never been on vinyl, and the Dylan cover, "You Ain't Going Nowhere."

yt: Live at Sleeping Village, Chicago, Sept 25, 2025
years.h: Silkworm go back on the road for the first time since 2005
years.p: The reunited band, with Joel Phelps and Jeff Panall, starts its first tour since Michael Dahlquist's death.
